newsitem.title: USA: Tosco says gas leak hits California refinery.
newsitem.headline: Tosco says gas leak hits California refinery.

text.p: U.S. Tosco Corp said it cut back to minimum levels some refining processes at its 104,000 barrel per day (bpd) plant in Rodeo, California on Wednesday night after a problem with a sulphur processing unit caused an escape of gases, a company spokesman said.
Tosco spokesman David Kory said there was "an upset" at a sulfur processing unit at the refinery, 25 miles (40 kms) northeast of San Francisco.
"It triggered depressurization of the unit," he said. Excess product went to the flare, acting as a safety valve, which burned the product off, he said.
"The unit is depressured ... Other refining processes have been cut back to a minimum," he said.
Kory said the coker and the hydrocracker were running at minimum levels but other hydrogen units continued to process normally.

He could not say what the impact on refinery operations would be, saying that would depend "on how long it takes to fix the problem." The cause of the problem was being investigated, but "could have been a pressure imbalance," he said.

Tosco sounded the community alert network, which warns local residents of problems at area refineries, because of a release of sulfur dioxide and another chemical which sent a rotten egg smell throughout the area.

Local health officials warned residents of the area to stay indoors and close doors and windows because of the release, but Kory said the chemicals were not concentrated enough to pose a hazard to human health.
Kory said the refinery had "no reports of any injuries or adverse effects" from the incident.

He said the leak was unrelated to another incident at the same refinery Wednesday morning when there was a brief fire at a processing unit that had been taken down for maintenance. The fire was extinguished without disrupting operations.
Tosco recently bought the refinery from Unocal Corp along with the company's other downstream assets.
